biomarkers.name: Hormonal secretion profile
biomarkers.clinical_use: Prolactinoma (prolactin), acromegaly (GH/IGF-1), Cushing disease (ACTH/cortisol), TSH-oma. Non-functioning: silent variants. Guides medical therapy (cabergoline for prolactinoma, somatostatin analogues for GH/TSH)

biomarkers.name: Transcription factor lineage (PIT1, SF-1, T-PIT)
biomarkers.clinical_use: WHO 2022 uses TF lineage for classification (PIT1: GH/PRL/TSH; SF-1: gonadotroph; T-PIT: corticotroph)

biomarkers.name: Ki-67, mitotic count, p53
biomarkers.clinical_use: Higher proliferative activity and extensive p53 staining are associated with more aggressive behaviour, but no single validated grading cutoff is sufficient alone; used with radiologic invasion and clinical course when considering closer follow-up or adjuvant therapy

biomarkers.name: MEN1 (germline)
biomarkers.prevalence: Subset of pituitary adenomas; pituitary tumours occur in ~30-40% of MEN1 patients

biomarkers.name: AIP (germline)
biomarkers.prevalence: Subset of familial isolated pituitary adenoma; found in ~15-30% of FIPA families
biomarkers.clinical_use: Genetic counselling in young acromegaly / gigantism or familial cases

biomarkers.name: USP8 mutations (Cushing)
biomarkers.prevalence: ~20-60% of corticotroph adenomas causing Cushing disease

biomarkers.name: GNAS mutations
biomarkers.clinical_use: Common driver in GH-secreting somatotroph tumours; supports molecular subtyping

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Sheets, cords, or nested growth of monomorphic cells with variable cytoplasm; classification by hormone lineage rather than morphology
variants: by lineage: PIT1 (GH/PRL/TSH), SF-1 (gonadotroph, mostly silent), T-PIT (corticotroph)
by hormone: prolactinoma, somatotroph, corticotroph, thyrotroph, gonadotroph, null cell
by aggressiveness: typical, atypical, pituitary carcinoma
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Renamed 'pituitary neuroendocrine tumours' (PitNET) in WHO 2022; there is no formal WHO grading system based solely on Ki-67, mitoses, and p53. The former 'atypical adenoma' category was removed; proliferation markers are used as adjunct prognostic features

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Not well characterised; likely reflects endocrine cell of origin

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Anterior pituitary cell types with distinct lineages: lactotrophs (prolactin), somatotrophs (GH), corticotrophs (ACTH), gonadotrophs (LH/FSH), thyrotrophs (TSH); each with distinct transcription factor programme (Pit-1 for lactotroph/somatotroph/thyrotroph; T-Pit for corticotroph; SF-1 for gonadotroph)
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Oral ectoderm (Rathke's pouch); the anterior pituitary derives from oral ectoderm invagination, distinct from the neurohypophysis of neuroectodermal origin
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Retains differentiation programme of cell of origin with hormone-specific transcription factors (Pit-1, T-Pit, SF-1) and hormone production; classification is now transcription-factor-based rather than immunohistochemistry-based alone
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Modern WHO classification recognises lineage-based tumour subtypes: Pit-1 lineage tumours (somatotroph, lactotroph, mammosomatotroph, mixed somatotroph-lactotroph, thyrotroph, plurihormonal Pit-1-positive), T-Pit lineage (corticotroph), SF-1 lineage (gonadotroph), null cell
